mainTopic: Spending on שבת and יום טוב, the gift of שבת, and which foods can serve as עירובי תבשילין
overview: The גמרא teaches that a person's income for the year is set between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. The exception is what he spends on שבת, יום טוב, and his sons' תלמוד תורה, which Heaven adds back to him. רבי אבהו finds the source in תהלים, and the גמרא proves that the word חק means food. A ברייתא then contrasts שמאי הזקן, who saved the best food all week for שבת, with הלל הזקן, who trusted that ה׳ blesses each day. Next the גמרא discusses whether a giver must tell the receiver about a gift. It explains that ה׳ told ישראל about the gift of שבת because its reward, or the נשמה יתירה, would stay hidden. Returning to the משנה, אביי rules that עירובי תבשילין needs a cooked dish and not bread, and two versions explain why, using porridge as the test case. The amud ends with small foods that can serve as the עירוב, and with salted fish cooked by a גוי. The answer to the last question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Yearly income is set, with three exceptions
steps.stepSummary: A person's income is fixed from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים, except for spending on שבת, יום טוב, and his sons' תלמוד תורה. For these, Heaven gives him more if he spends more and less if he spends less.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of a person's food and income for the year is set for him between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. The exceptions are what he spends on שבת, on יום טוב, and on his sons' תורה learning. For these, if he spends less, he is given less, and if he spends more, he is given more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: how much a person earns in a year is decided at the start of the year, but spending on three special things is not limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of a person's income is fixed in advance, so spending more will not bring him more. For שבת, יום טוב, and תלמוד תורה, Heaven matches his spending. So a person does not lose by spending generously on these.

keyTerms.meaning: his food, meaning his livelihood or income
learning תורה (here, paying for one's children to learn)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a person's whole income grows if he spends more on anything he likes. Only spending on these three things is matched by Heaven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why a person need not hold back on spending for שבת and יום טוב. Heaven will cover what he spends on them.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם קְצוּבִים לוֹ
phrases.english: All of a person's livelihood is fixed for him
from Rosh HaShana until Yom Kippur,
except for expenses for Shabbatot
and expenses for Yom Tov
and expenses for his sons' Torah study,
for if he reduced, they reduce for him,
and if he added, they add for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם קְצוּבִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about spending on שבת and יום טוב with a general rule about income.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Income is set on ראש השנה, but spending on שבת, יום טוב, and תלמוד תורה is matched by Heaven.

steps.title: רבי אבהו finds the source in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a פסוק showing that ראש השנה is the festival when the moon is hidden. The next פסוק calls it a חק, a fixed allotment, for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is the פסוק for this? 'Blow the שופר at the new moon, at the hidden time, for our festival day.' Which festival has a hidden moon? It must be ראש השנה. And the next פסוק says: 'For it is a חק for ישראל, a judgment of the God of יעקב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו asks where the rule comes from and answers with two פסוקים in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only ראש השנה falls on the first of the month, when the moon cannot yet be seen. The next פסוק calls that day a חק and a משפט. So on ראש השנה a person's חק, his allotment, is judged and set.

keyTerms.meaning: at the hidden time, when the moon is covered
you must say, it can only be
a fixed portion; here understood as an allotment of food

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: What is the verse?
"Blow the shofar at the new moon
at the hidden time, for our festival day,"
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It means 'when the moon is hidden'.

phrases.english: which festival is it when the moon is hidden?
You must say this is Rosh HaShana,
and it is written: "For it is a statute for Israel,
a judgment of the God of Jacob."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That income is judged and set on ראש השנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 81:4-5: ראש השנה is called a חק and a משפט.

steps.title: How do we know חק means food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word חק in the פסוק refers to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word 'חק' is a word about food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions one link in רבי אבהו's proof. It is setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's proof only works if חק means a food allotment. Normally חק means a law or statute, so the גמרא asks for evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: how is it implied, how do we know

phrases.english: How do we know that this word "statute"
is a term for food?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי חֹק לִישָּׁנָא דִּמְזוֹנֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a key word in the proof of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that חק means a portion of food.

steps.title: Proof from the food פרעה gave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from בראשית that חק means a food portion: the כהנים of מצרים ate the חק that פרעה gave them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they ate their חק that פרעה gave them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק where חק plainly means food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, people 'eat' their חק, so the word must mean a portion of food. This shows that חק in תהלים can mean an allotment of food too.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And they ate their allotment
which Pharaoh gave them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In בראשית 47:22 the word חק is something eaten, so it means food.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's proof from משלי
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a different פסוק: 'Feed me my allotted bread' (לחם חקי).
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: We learn it from here: 'Feed me my allotted bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a second source showing that חק means food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word חק is attached directly to bread, לחם חקי. This also shows that חק means a portion of food. Both answers reach the same result through different פסוקים.
steps.whatToRemember: ראש השנה is called a חק, and חק means a food allotment. So a person's food and income for the year are decided on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: From here:
"Feed me my allotted bread."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question as step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In משלי 30:8, חק is connected to bread, so it means food.

steps.title: How שמאי הזקן honored שבת all week
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says שמאי הזקן ate all week in honor of שבת. Whenever he found a nicer animal, he saved it for שבת and ate the one he had saved before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: They said about שמאי הזקן that all his days he ate in honor of שבת. If he found a nice animal, he said, 'This is for שבת.' If he then found a nicer one, he set aside the second one for שבת and ate the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing שמאי הזקן's way of honoring שבת all week long. It connects to the earlier theme of spending for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי always kept the best animal he had for שבת. When he found a better one, he ate the old one, so even his weekday meals were part of honoring שבת. This shows how highly he valued spending on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: שמאי did not save every animal for שבת. He kept only the best one for שבת and ate the earlier one during the week.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן,
phrases.english: It was taught: They said about Shammai the Elder

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו הָיָה אוֹכֵל לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: that all his days he would eat in honor of Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא בְּהֵמָה נָאָה, אוֹמֵר: זוֹ לַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: If he found a nice animal, he would say: This is for Shabbat.
If he found another one nicer than it,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְאוֹכֵל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.english: he would set aside the second and eat the first.
phrases.notes: He kept the nicer, second animal for שבת, so eating the first one was also for the sake of שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about spending on שבת to a story of a great person who lived by it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי הזקן always kept the best food for שבת, so all his eating during the week honored שבת.

steps.title: Hillel's different way: trusting each day
steps.stepSummary: Unlike שמאי, הלל הזקן did not save the best food all week for שבת. All his actions were for the sake of Heaven, trusting that ה׳ gives blessing day by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But הלל הזקן had a different trait: all his actions were for the sake of Heaven, as it says, 'Blessed is ה׳, day by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues past שמאי's practice and shows that הלל had a different approach to preparing for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי kept setting aside the best animal for שבת. הלל did not worry about this. He trusted that ה׳ would send something good for שבת when the time came, so he could eat each day without stockpiling.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל the Elder, the great teacher who lived at the same time as שמאי
A different trait or way of acting
Day by day, meaning each day gets its own blessing

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean הלל cared less about honoring שבת. It means he trusted that ה׳ would provide for שבת when it came.

phrases.english: But Hillel the Elder
had a different trait,
that all his actions were for the sake of Heaven,
as it says: "Blessed is ה׳, day by day."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts הלל's approach with שמאי's practice in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל trusted in daily blessing from ה׳ and did not stockpile for שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the same dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the story: בית שמאי say to prepare for שבת starting from the first day of the week, while בית הלל say 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: בית שמאי say, from the first day of your week, prepare for your שבת. בית הלל say, 'Blessed is ה׳, day by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the difference between שמאי and הלל was also a dispute between their schools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story was about two individuals. This ברייתא shows the same two approaches as general positions of בית שמאי and בית הלל, which confirms the story.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a ברייתא that supports what was just said
From the first day of your week (Sunday)

steps.whatToRemember: שמאי's way: plan for שבת all week long. הלל's way: trust that ה׳ blesses each day.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Beis Shammai say:
From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbos,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: ״בָּרוּךְ ה׳ יוֹם יוֹם״.
phrases.english: and Beis Hillel say: "Blessed is ה׳, day by day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The contrast between שמאי's and הלל's approaches to preparing for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the positions of בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: A giver does not need to tell the receiver
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that someone who gives a gift does not need to tell the receiver. He learns this from משה, who did not know that his face was shining.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: someone who gives a gift to his friend does not need to tell him, as it says, 'And משה did not know that the skin of his face shone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about gifts. It stays on the theme of שבת because שבת will come up as a gift in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ gave משה a shining face and did not tell him, so משה did not know about it. From this רבי חמא learns that a giver does not need to announce his gift.

keyTerms.meaning: The skin of his face shone

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
One who gives a gift to his friend
does not need to let him know,
as it says: "And Moshe did not know
that the skin of his face shone."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, linked to the theme of שבת and honoring it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A giver does not need to tell the receiver about the gift.

steps.title: Challenge: ה׳ told משה to announce שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חמא‎. ה׳ told משה to inform ישראל about the gift of שבת, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from this that someone who gives bread to a child must tell the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from the פסוק 'to know that I am ה׳ who makes you holy.' הקב״ה said to משה: 'I have a good gift in My treasure house, and its name is שבת. I want to give it to ישראל. Go and tell them.' From here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: someone who gives bread to a child must tell his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to say the opposite of רבי חמא: a giver should tell the receiver about the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ made a point of having משה announce the gift of שבת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even turns this into a rule about giving bread to a child. That clashes directly with רבי חמא's teaching that there is no need to tell.

phrases.english: They challenged:
"To know that I am ה׳ who makes you holy,"
phrases.notes: שמות 31:13, a פסוק about keeping שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: מֹשֶׁה!
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed is He, said to Moshe: Moshe!

phrases.aramaic: מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי
phrases.english: I have a good gift in My treasure house
and its name is Shabbos,
and I want to give it to the Jewish people;
go and let them know.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
One who gives bread to a child
must let his mother know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חמא's rule from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חמא's rule that a giver does not need to tell the receiver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ had the gift of שבת announced, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires telling a child's mother. Both show that a giver should inform the receiver.

steps.title: Gifts that will be noticed versus hidden gifts
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. A gift that will become known by itself does not need to be announced. A gift that will not become known on its own does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is about a gift that will become known by itself, and that case is about a gift that will not become known by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by dividing gifts into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's shining face was going to be noticed anyway, since people would see it, so there was no need to tell him. When a gift would stay hidden, the giver should tell. So both sources are right, each about a different kind of gift.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; both sources can be true

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about a gift that will become known by itself,
phrases.notes: This refers to משה's shining face, the case where there was no need to tell.

phrases.english: that is about a gift that will not become known by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source talks about a different kind of gift
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to give opposite rules about every gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: If a gift will be noticed anyway, the giver need not announce it. If it will stay hidden, he should tell.

steps.title: But שבת will also become known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: שבת itself is a gift that would become known anyway, so why did it need to be announced?
steps.simpleTranslation: But שבת is also a gift that would become known by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, because שבת seems to fit the 'will become known' category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל would eventually be taught all about שבת, so it seems to be a gift that becomes known on its own. Under the new rule, ה׳ should not have needed to tell משה to announce it.

phrases.english: Shabbos too is a gift that will become known by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between gifts that become known and hidden gifts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת would become known anyway, yet ה׳ still had it announced.

steps.title: The reward of שבת stays hidden
steps.stepSummary: The commandment of שבת would become known, but its reward would not. That hidden reward is why ה׳ had it announced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The giving of its reward would not become known by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hidden part of the gift of שבת is its reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone would learn the laws of שבת. But how great the reward for keeping it is would never be seen on its own. Since that part stays hidden, ה׳ had to tell ישראל about it.
steps.whatToRemember: A giver must tell the receiver only about a gift that would otherwise stay hidden. With שבת, the hidden part is its reward.

phrases.english: Its reward will not become known by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a hidden part of the gift
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת seemed to be a gift that would be fully known anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reward of שבת stays hidden, so it needed to be announced.

steps.title: How does the giver let the mother know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule again and asks how the giver actually tells the child's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: From here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learned that one who gives bread to a child must inform his mother. What does he do to the child to inform her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule from step 10 and asks a practical question: how is the mother told? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 only said that the mother must be told. Now the גמרא wants to know the method. The giver usually does not speak to the mother himself, so there has to be a sign she will notice.

keyTerms.meaning: To inform, to let someone know
What does he do to him?

phrases.english: The Master said,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: from here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
phrases.notes: "From here" means from ה׳ telling משה to let ישראל know about שבת (step 10).

phrases.english: One who gives bread to a child
must inform his mother.
What does he do to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule quoted in step 10 to explain how it works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical way the giver lets the mother know about the gift.

steps.title: Oil and eye paint as a sign
steps.stepSummary: The giver rubs oil on the child and puts eye paint on him, so the mother will notice and ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: He rubs oil on the child and puts eye paint on his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the giver marks the child with oil and eye paint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the mother sees the oil and eye paint, she will ask what happened. That is how she learns that someone was kind to her child. The sign does the telling, so the giver does not have to speak to her.

phrases.english: He rubs oil on him
and fills his eyes with eye paint.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁיֵיף לֵיהּ מִשְׁחָא וּמָלֵי לֵיהּ כּוּחְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The giver marks the child with oil and eye paint so the mother notices.

steps.title: What about today, when people fear witchcraft?
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays people worry that marks on a child could be witchcraft, so what should the giver do?
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when we are worried about witchcraft, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If marking the child with eye paint makes people suspect witchcraft, the old method no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother might be frightened instead of grateful if she finds strange paint on her child. So the גמרא needs a sign that will not cause that worry.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when we are concerned about witchcraft,
what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a practical problem with the method given in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A way to let the mother know that will not look like witchcraft.

steps.title: Rub on some of the same food
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the giver should rub on the child a bit of the same food he gave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He rubs on the child some of that same type of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new method for today: mark the child with a little of the food itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bit of the same food on the child clearly shows that someone fed him, and it does not look like witchcraft. The goal stays the same as in step 15: the mother should find out about the gift. Only the sign changes.
steps.whatToRemember: A giver should make sure the receiver's family can find out about the gift, through a sign that is clear and does not cause worry.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
He rubs on him from that same type.
phrases.notes: He means a little of the same food that was given with the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁיֵיף לֵיהּ מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mark the child with a little of the same food instead of eye paint.

steps.title: שבת was given privately
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, teaches that all מצוות were given publicly except שבת, which was given privately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: All the מצוות that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to ישראל He gave publicly, except שבת, which He gave privately, as it says: "Between Me and the children of ישראל it is a sign forever."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the gift of שבת: it was given in private, unlike every other מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "between Me and the children of ישראל" show that שבת is a personal sign between ה׳ and the Jewish people, like a private gift. This continues the theme of שבת as a special gift from earlier in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, blessed be He

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
All the מצוות that He gave to them,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel,
He gave them in public,
except for Shabbat, which He gave them in private,
as it is stated: "Between Me and the children of Israel
it is a sign forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching on the theme of שבת as ה׳'s gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מצוה was given publicly except שבת, which was given privately, as a sign between ה׳ and ישראל.

steps.title: Then how can גוים be held responsible?
steps.stepSummary: If שבת was given privately, the גוים should not be punished in connection with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the גוים should not be punished about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 18: something given in secret should not make anyone outside the secret responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת was hidden from the world, the גוים never really knew about it. So it seems unfair for them to be punished for anything to do with it. Yet the גמרא assumes they are held responsible, so it needs an answer.

phrases.english: If so,
the gentiles should not be punished for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לָא לִעַנְשׁוּ גּוֹיִם עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 18 that שבת was given privately.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's statement that שבת was given in private.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A secret gift cannot be the basis for holding outsiders responsible, yet the גוים are held responsible about שבת.

steps.title: שבת was told, its reward was not
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ did tell the world about שבת itself, but He kept its reward private.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבת itself He did tell them about. The reward for keeping it He did not tell them about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that only the reward of שבת was kept secret, not שבת itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוים knew about שבת, so they can be held responsible. The "private" part is the reward, which ה׳ shared only with ישראל. This matches step 13, where the reward was the hidden part of the gift.

phrases.english: Shabbat, He did inform them of,
its reward, He did not inform them of.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole מצוה of שבת was kept secret from the world.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת was made known to all; only its reward was kept for ישראל.

steps.title: Another answer: the extra soul was kept secret
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even the reward was told, but the נשמה יתירה was kept secret.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: He told them about its reward too, but about the extra soul He did not tell them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge of step 19, naming a different hidden part of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers agree that שבת itself was public. They only disagree about what the private part is: the reward (step 20) or the נשמה יתירה (this step). The next step explains what the נשמה יתירה is.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
An extra soul given on שבת

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
its reward too He informed them of,
the additional soul, He did not inform them of.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ נָמֵי אוֹדְעִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 19, offered alongside step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer naming a different hidden element
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reward was the secret part of שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reward may have been told too; the secret part is the נשמה יתירה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש on the extra soul of שבת
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that ה׳ gives a person an extra soul on ערב שבת and takes it back at מוצאי שבת, learned from "שבת וינפש".
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: The Holy One, blessed be He, gives a person an extra soul on ערב שבת, and at מוצאי שבת it is taken from him, as it says: "He rested and was refreshed (וינפש)." Once he has rested, woe, the soul is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's teaching as the source for the נשמה יתירה mentioned in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads וַיִּנָּפַשׁ as two words: וַוי (woe) and נֶפֶשׁ (soul). When שבת ends, the extra soul leaves, and that is a loss. This shows that the נשמה יתירה is a real, hidden gift of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve of שבת, Friday before שבת
The end of שבת, Saturday night
"And was refreshed"; read here as וַוי נֶפֶשׁ, "woe, the soul"

steps.whatToRemember: שבת was given to everyone openly, but part of it stayed private between ה׳ and ישראל: either its reward, or the נשמה יתירה that comes on ערב שבת and leaves at מוצאי שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The קרא does not say "woe" in its simple meaning. ריש לקיש is splitting the word וַיִּנָּפַשׁ to read a hidden message into it.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נוֹתֵן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: An additional soul the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives
in a person on Shabbat eve,
and at the conclusion of Shabbat they take it from him,
as it is stated: "He rested and was refreshed,"
once he has rested,
woe, the soul is lost.
phrases.notes: Here וַיִּנָּפַשׁ is split into וַוי (woe) and נֶפֶשׁ (soul).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer of step 21 by showing where the idea of a נשמה יתירה comes from.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that there is a hidden נשמה יתירה on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's reading of "שבת וינפש" (שמות 31:17) as וַוי נֶפֶשׁ.

steps.title: אביי: only a cooked dish works, not bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about making a cooked dish on ערב יום טוב, and אביי limits it: the עירוב must be a cooked dish, and bread alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a person makes a cooked dish on the eve of יום טוב. אביי said: they only taught this about a cooked dish, but bread does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה and brings אביי's rule that עירובי תבשילין needs a real cooked dish, not just bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'תבשיל', a cooked dish. אביי reads that word strictly: bread, even though it is baked food, cannot count. This sets up the question of why bread is worse.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם תַּבְשִׁיל מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: A person makes a cooked dish on the eve of the Festival.
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from our משנה. The גמרא is coming back to it after the long side discussion.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They taught this only about a cooked dish,
but bread, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא תַּבְשִׁיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה about שבת to the משנה's הלכה of עירובי תבשילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עירובי תבשילין requires a cooked dish; bread alone does not work.

steps.title: Why is bread different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes bread unfit for the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about bread that it does not work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's rule. This question sets up the next moves, where reasons are suggested and tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is real, filling food, so it is not obvious why it fails. The גמרא wants the reason so it can know which other foods work.

phrases.english: What is different about bread, that it does not work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind אביי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason bread cannot serve as עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: Is the reason that the food must go with bread? Porridge disproves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the עירוב must be something eaten with bread. It rejects this because porridge is also not eaten with bread, yet porridge works for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we need something that goes along with bread, and bread does not go with itself, then porridge also does not go with bread. רבי זירא said: those foolish Babylonians eat bread with bread, meaning bread with porridge. Yet רב נחומי בר זכריה said in אביי's name that one may make an עירוב with porridge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reason, that an עירוב must be a side dish for bread. It then attacks that reason using porridge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא shows that porridge counts like bread, not like a side dish. So under this reason porridge should fail. But אביי himself, as reported by רב נחומי, allows porridge. So this cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Something eaten along with bread, a side dish

phrases.english: If you say we need something that accompanies bread,
and bread does not accompany bread,
but porridge also does not accompany bread,
as Rabbi Zeira said:
Those foolish Babylonians
who eat bread with bread.
phrases.notes: He means they eat bread with porridge. Porridge is grain food, so it's like eating bread with more bread.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: And Rav Neḥumi bar Zekharya said in the name of Abaye:
One may make an eiruv with porridge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason that an עירוב must be a food eaten with bread.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Porridge is not eaten with bread (רבי זירא), so this reason would rule it out, yet אביי allows porridge.

steps.title: The real reason: the food must be unusual
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an עירוב must be something not eaten every day. Bread is everyday food, but porridge is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we need something that is not common. Bread is common, and porridge is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason that fits both אביי's rule about bread and his ruling about porridge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since bread is eaten all the time, setting it aside does not show that it is meant for the עירוב. Porridge is less ordinary, so setting it aside is noticeable. This explains why porridge works and bread does not.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: an עירוב must be something unusual. Bread is too ordinary, so it fails, but porridge works.

phrases.english: Rather, we need something that is not common,
and bread is common,
and porridge is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with one that fits אביי's ruling on porridge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason offered in place of the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב must be a food eaten with bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב must be an unusual food; bread is ordinary, porridge is not.

steps.title: Second version: אביי's same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version of the discussion, starting again with אביי's rule that bread does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אביי said, they only taught this about a cooked dish, but bread does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates אביי's rule to begin a second version of the discussion. It is setting up a different chain of reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is the same. What changes in this version is what רב נחומי reported about porridge, and so the reason will change too.

phrases.english: Some say:
Abaye said:
They taught this only about a cooked dish,
but bread, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second version of the same discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread alone cannot serve as עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the גמרא again asks why bread does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's rule, setting up the next attempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same question as before, but this time the evidence about porridge will point in the other direction.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for the rule just restated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why bread cannot serve as עירובי תבשילין, in the second version.

steps.title: Is the reason that the food must be unusual? Porridge disproves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is that bread is too ordinary, but rejects it because porridge is unusual, and yet in this version אביי rules porridge does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we need something uncommon, and bread is common, then porridge is uncommon. Yet רב נחומי בר זכריה said in אביי's name that one may not make an עירוב with porridge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the 'unusual food' reason and knocks it down using porridge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב נחומי reports that porridge does not work. If the reason were 'unusual food', porridge should work. So the reason must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: We may not make an עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions report opposite rulings from אביי about porridge. In the first, porridge works; in this one, it does not. That is why each version ends up with a different reason.

phrases.english: If you say that we need something that is not common,
and bread is common,
but porridge is not common,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: and Rav Neḥumi bar Zekharya said in the name of Abaye:
One may not make an eiruv with porridge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests the 'unusual food' answer and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason that an עירוב must be an unusual food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Porridge is unusual, so it should work, yet in this version אביי rules porridge cannot be used.

steps.title: The real reason: the food must go with bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an עירוב must be something eaten with bread. Neither bread nor porridge is, as רבי זירא's remark shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we need something that goes along with bread. Bread does not go with bread, and porridge also does not go with bread, as רבי זירא said: those foolish Babylonians eat bread with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason that fits this version: the עירוב must be a side dish eaten with bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי זירא's remark is used as support: porridge is like bread, not a side dish. So both bread and porridge fail, matching רב נחומי's report in this version.
steps.whatToRemember: Second version: an עירוב must be a food eaten with bread. Bread and porridge both fail.

phrases.english: Rather, we need something that accompanies bread,
and bread does not accompany bread,
and porridge also does not accompany bread.
As Rabbi Zeira said:
Those foolish Babylonians
who eat bread with bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with one that fits this version's ruling on porridge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason offered in place of the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב must be an unusual food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב must be a food eaten with bread; bread and porridge both fail.

steps.title: Leftover lentils at the bottom of a pot
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that lentils left at the bottom of a pot can be used for עירובי תבשילין, as long as there is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: lentils at the bottom of a pot, one may rely on them for עירובי תבשילין. This is only when there is a כזית of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: even leftover food not set aside on purpose can count as the cooked dish for the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lentils were cooked anyway, so they are a real cooked dish. The גמרא adds a minimum amount: there must be at least a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: The cooked-food עירוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת
The size of an olive, a minimum amount

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
Lentils that are at the bottom of a pot,
one may rely on them as the joining of cooked foods.
And this applies only when there is an olive-bulk of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which foods qualify to a case of leftover food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover lentils at the bottom of a pot work for עירובי תבשילין if there is a כזית.

steps.title: Fat scraped off a knife
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה teaches that fat on a knife can be scraped off and used for עירובי תבשילין, as long as there is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק the son of רב יהודה said: fat on a knife, one scrapes it off and relies on it for עירובי תבשילין. This is only when there is a כזית of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A similar teaching: even a small leftover like fat on a knife can serve as the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the lentils, this shows the cooked dish does not need to be a full, prepared portion. The same minimum of a כזית applies.
steps.whatToRemember: Even leftovers, like lentils in a pot or fat on a knife, can be the עירובי תבשילין, as long as there is a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:
Fat that is on a knife,
one scrapes it off and relies on it
as the joining of cooked foods.
And this applies only when there is an olive-bulk of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to רבי חייא's lentils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat scraped from a knife works for עירובי תבשילין if there is a כזית.

steps.title: Small salted fish are not considered food cooked by a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רב: small salted fish that a גוי cooked do not fall under the prohibition of בישולי גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רב: Small salted fish are not subject to the prohibition of food cooked by non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב about small salted fish. Even if a גוי cooked them, they are not forbidden as בישולי גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of בישולי גוים is about food that only becomes edible through cooking. Small salted fish can already be eaten after salting, so the גוי's cooking does not really make them into food. That is why the prohibition does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Food cooked by a non-Jew, which the רבנן forbade
The rule of ___ does not apply to them

phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rav said:
Small salted fish
phrases.notes: He means small salted fish that a non-Jew then cooked.

phrases.english: are not subject to the prohibition of food cooked by non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of food rulings (lentils, knife fat) with a new food case that connects to עירובי תבשילין in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small salted fish cooked by a גוי are not forbidden as בישולי גוים.

steps.title: Roasted salted fish can be used for the עירוב, but a fancy fried dish is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that if a גוי roasted the small salted fish, a Jew may use them for עירובי תבשילין. But if the גוי made them into כסא דהרסנא, they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And if a non-Jew roasted them, one may rely on them for עירובי תבשילין. But if a non-Jew made them into a dish of fish fried with oil and flour, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף builds on רב's ruling. Roasted fish are still allowed, and can even serve as the עירוב, but turning them into a fancy fried dish makes them forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple roasting does not change the fish into a new kind of food, so it is still not בישולי גוים. Frying them with oil and flour makes an important dish, and that kind of cooking does fall under בישולי גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of small fish fried in oil and flour

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Roasting keeps the fish permitted, and they can even be used for the עירוב. Frying them into כסא דהרסנא makes them forbidden to eat altogether.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
And if a non-Jew roasted them,
one may rely on them for the joining of cooked foods.
But if a non-Jew made them into
fish fried with oil and flour, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וְאִם צְלָאָן גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב's ruling: the fish are not just permitted to eat but can also serve as the עירוב, with a limit for a fancy fried dish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted fish roasted by a גוי may be used for עירובי תבשילין. If he made them into כסא דהרסנא, they are forbidden.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last part of רב יוסף's ruling: of course fish that a גוי made into כסא דהרסנא, a cooked dish of fish fried in oil and flour, are forbidden. Why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף needed to say that כסא דהרסנא made by a גוי is forbidden, since that seems obvious. The next step begins the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dish of fish fried with oil and flour is clearly a real cooked dish made by a גוי, so it seems obvious that it falls under בישולי גוים. The גמרא assumes every teaching should add something new, so it looks for what we might have mistakenly thought.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the prohibition of כסא דהרסנא at the end of step 34 needed to be stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that salted fish a גוי made into כסא דהרסנא are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fried dish of fish, oil and flour is plainly something a גוי cooked into a new food, so of course it is forbidden. Saying so seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Starting to explain what we might have thought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'מהו דתימא': you might have thought otherwise. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer. The גמרא is about to explain the mistaken idea that רב יוסף's teaching was needed to correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מהו דתימא introduces a possible wrong assumption that makes the teaching necessary. The actual content of that assumption comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said or thought
